summary: Case report of recurrent aortic false aneurysm in Behcet's disease repaired with a Dacron bypass graft; no plastic particles studied.
Retrospective series of silver-coated Dacron in-situ revascularisation for secondary aorto-enteric fistulae; no plastic particles studied.
Oral PBAT microplastics in mice depleted butyrate-producing gut bacteria, impaired the colonic barrier and were associated with hippocampal microglial lipotoxicity and memory loss.
Polyethylene microplastics fed to mice for four months accumulated in the cochlea and vestibule, raised hearing thresholds and altered balance behaviour and cortical glucose metabolism.
Biocompatibility of calcium peroxide-loaded polycaprolactone microparticles as an oxygen-releasing carrier for osteogenic stem cell culture and tissue engineering.
Autopsy series of infective endocarditis on Dacron patches after congenital heart defect repair; no plastic particles studied.
Dietary PP and PET micro and nanoplastics reduced thyroid function in adolescent mice, with gut microbiota changes and HPT axis disruption implicated via faecal transplantation.
Review of early-onset colorectal cancer aetiology covering metabolic dysfunction, microbiome and exposome factors; micro- and nanoplastics mentioned only briefly.
True-to-life PET nanoplastics from water bottles were internalised by primary human nasal epithelial cells, raising ROS, reducing mitochondrial membrane potential and altering autophagy markers.
Microplastics were detected in human endometrium; in mice they reached the uterus, reduced fertility and caused endometrial inflammation, and induced apoptosis in endometrial organoids.
Sulfonate-modified polystyrene nanoparticles at 1-100 ug/L caused transgenerational locomotion and reproductive toxicity in C. elegans mediated by germline Notch signalling.
Lanthanide-labelled polystyrene nanoplastics traced in mice showed low oral translocation, liver and spleen accumulation after injection, and retention in iron-rich brain areas.
Randomised crossover trial comparing calcium and sodium polystyrene sulfonate binders on mineral metabolism in hyperkalaemic pre-dialysis patients.
Prospective series of Prolene mesh repair for incarcerated or strangulated ventral hernias; no plastic particles studied.
Survey of microplastics in gastrointestinal tracts of stranded Indus River dolphins with polymer risk assessment; no health endpoint measured.
Pig study comparing polypropylene mesh structures at the oesophageal hiatus for shrinkage, adhesions and tissue integration; bulk implant only.
Randomised trial of low-dose cholestyramine as adjunctive therapy in hyperthyroid Graves' disease.
Field survey of plastic ingestion in Mediterranean catsharks with exploratory splenic immune gene expression; wildlife survey without controlled exposure.
Network toxicology and docking predicted links between PET microplastic degradation products and migrants and biomineralisation disorders such as kidney stones and vascular calcification.
Bioimprinted polymethacrylate and polystyrene culture substrates used to study topography effects on Ishikawa endometrial cancer cells.
Review of potassium-binding agents including sodium polystyrene sulfonate for hyperkalaemia during RAAS inhibitor therapy.
Microplastics were detected in all 18 human tissue types from ten donors, highest in adipose, brain, adrenal, liver and thyroid and lowest in blood.
Palladium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics were traced by mass cytometry in human blood immune cell subsets, affecting function, and accumulated in immune cells of mouse liver and spleen.
Hybrid lipid-latex nanoparticles developed for imaging and drug delivery targeting inflammatory macrophages in atherosclerosis and obesity models.
In crayfish, 5 and 100 um microplastics accumulated in gills and gut, enhanced copper uptake and, combined with copper, worsened hepatopancreatic damage and oxidative stress.
